detail: Both corpus texts ingested from .txt with `lc ingest` and indexed with `lc anchor` (doc-control segment over the converted .docx, novel profile, work language); detected chapter starts compared with the gold heading lines in tests/fixtures/gold/chapters.json. Plain text carries no styles, so the .txt reader now writes plain text's heading convention (a short line with two or more extra blank lines above it and a blank line below) as Heading 1; doc-control's heading_style signal does the rest. scene_boundary_f1 over the nine variants of tests/test_anchor.py stays 1.0.

differences_from_old_detector.chapter_starts: none: the same 10 and 22 chapter starts as structure.detect gave
differences_from_old_detector.chapter_titles: Jekyll and Hyde: none. Marianela: 19 of 22 titles equal the old detector's ('-I- Perdido'), now from doc-control's heading_last; the other 3 gain a subtitle the old detector left out as too long ('-III-' is now '-III- Un diálogo que servirá de exposición'; also -X- and -XVIII-)
differences_from_old_detector.anchors: Jekyll and Hyde: 0 of 350 change. Marianela: 154 of 1,270 change, all inside those 3 chapters (the subtitle line moves from scene 1 to the heading block in scene 0)
differences_from_old_detector.scenes: same count (11 and 23); scene_style (an 'after break' paragraph style) opens a scene again and is recorded in structure.json signals
differences_from_old_detector.dropped_signals: short upper-case lines and numerals with no layout in a plain-text draft (kept through convert._txt_headings until doc-control's chapter_blank_lines, T50), an ornament under a chapter title staying in the heading block (needs doc-control's uncapped suppressed list, T50), the shallowest-heading-level choice for Markdown '##' chapters (doc-control chapter_level auto, T50)

timing: lc ingest + lc anchor, worst of three in-process runs: jekyll-hyde 0.13 s before, 0.18 s after; marianela 0.33 s before, 0.57 s after (anchor 0.07 s -> 0.22-0.29 s: the .docx is converted and parsed again for segment)
